reference.title: WH-guide JACE-8000, JACE-9000
reference.shortdesc: This content is reused in the JACE-8000 WiFi, JACE-9000 WiFi, JACE-8000 and JACE-9000 Startup guides.

refbody.section:
JACE-8000 notes, tables and paragraphsThe presence of a USB device inserted in the USB backup/restore port prevents you from accidentally launching the factory defaults recovery process while attempting to restore a backup. If a USB device, of any type, is inserted in the backup/restore port, recovery is skipped. Consequently, to recover factory defaults, no USB device can be inserted in the USB port.USB backup supports only FAT32 and FAT32X file systems. NTFS is not supported.Only flash drives (USB sticks ≤128GB) are recommended for backup/restore operations. USB bus powered external hard drives often have higher power requirements and so may not function as expected, possibly resulting in permanent damage to the drive or to the . Plugging in an external hard drive may cause the controller to become unresponsive, requiring a reboot. If you lose the system passphrase, you will lose access to the controller’s encrypted data.
Niagara 4 cannot successfully configure the system passphrase on the JACE8000 when it is running the daemon. You must use AX38U1 instead.
Also, in the Platform Administration view, the Update Authentication and System Passphrase buttons are disabled when the remote platform is the AX38U1 daemon. Note, that in release Niagara 4.1, the buttons do not show as disabled, however, setting the system passphrase fails when you attempt to configure it.When upgrading a JACE-8000 from an installed older release, the persistent log files under /var/slog are not preserved. The reason is that contains an OS upgrade from QNX6.5 to QNX7.0, which uses a different log file format. During the upgrade the old QNX6.5 log files are deleted and new QNX7.0 files are created. For any JACE-8000 that is converted to run , the 802.1X wired authentication standard is not supported This topic covers only those controller models that support battery backup. Starting in , the Data Recovery Service Editor view includes additional configurable properties. For example, Station Save Limit, Station Save Limit Period, Generate Alert on Replay and Platform Alarm Support. For any converted to run AX, USB Backup/Restore functionality is not supported. Also, the USB port on the device is not monitored for insertion/removal of devices. The can be converted (downgraded) to run with some feature limitations. For example, for any running AX the USB functionality is not supported. In this configuration the USB port on the device is not monitored for insertion/removal of devices. This does NOT apply to the . For any AX station with CryptoService that you attempt to upgrade to AX, once you commission the controller the station will fail to start after the successful upgrade. The same is true if you attempt to move an AX supervisor to an AX station and start it. As a preparatory step, manually remove CryptoService from the station’s Services directory before attempting to commission it.
WLAN capability of JACE-8000 models
Model nameFactory configurationWLAN capability
JACE-8000-CSE-001 USWLAN-enabledYou can turn on WiFi using the Selector Switch, and configure for US operation only.
JACE-8000-CSE-002 WWWLAN-enabledYou can turn on WiFi using the Selector Switch, and configure for countries other than the US.
JACE-8000-CSE-003 XXWLAN-not includedWiFi capability is not included with this model.
WLAN capability of JACE-9000 models
Model nameFactory configurationWLAN capability
JACE-8000-CSE-001 USWLAN-enabledYou can turn on WiFi using the Selector Switch, and configure for US operation only.
JACE-8000-CSE-002 WWWLAN-enabledYou can turn on WiFi using the Selector Switch, and configure for countries other than the US.
JACE-9000-CSE-003 XXWLAN-not includedWiFi capability is not included with this model.
JACE-8000 WiFi capability is pre-configured by the factory as either “WLAN-enabled” or “WLAN-disabled”. For models that are factory configured as WLAN-enabled (e.g. JACE-8000-CSE-001 US, JACE-8000-CSE-002 WW ), additional steps must be taken to configure the adapter. Conversely, for models that are factory-configured as WLAN-disabled (e.g. JACE-8000-CSE-003 XX), WiFi is permanently disabled. The WLAN adapter cannot be used or configured.
You can verify the WLAN factory configuration either with the product packaging or via the Serial Shell. If disabled, the packaging will be labeled with “WLAN DISABLED”, or “JACE-8000-CSE-003”, or with both. If packaging is already removed, you can check the configuration using the Serial Shell.
At the prompt in the Serial Shell Main Menu, type: sh.
The shell $ prompt opens.
At the $ prompt, type the command: wifi-skureadand press Enter.
This will return the one of the following codes for your device. The returned code indicates the device’s WLAN capability:
US =United States (WiFi enabled for the US only)
WW = World Wide (WiFi enabled for countries other than the US)
XX = Disabled (WiFi is permanently disabled)
the following note explains WiFi capability. for the XX model onlyFor factory-configured WLAN-disabled models only (for example, JACE-8000-CSE-003 XX), WiFi is permanently disabled. The WLAN adapter cannot be used or configured.Starting in , the JACE-8000 can be converted (downgraded) to run –with some feature limitations. For example, for any JACE-8000 running the WiFi functionality is not supported. In this configuration, the WiFi switch position on the device is not monitored. Other unsupported features are IEEE 802.1X wired authentication and USB backup/restore.

property.propvalue: Reports that access point processes are starting: the access point mode is enabled in the WiFi Configuration view and the three-position switch on the unit is in the ACC (left) position.
property.propdesc: This starts the WiFi driver, which adds a tiw_sap0 adapter, brings the adapter up and assigns an IP address to it, starts Hostapd, and starts the Dhcp server on the adapter. This state can only be entered from the Stopped state.

property.propvalue: In Access Point mode, a non-zero "Inactivity Timeout" has been configured, and for the specified amount of time the adapter neither sends nor receives non-broadcast packets to/from attached clients. The adapter is shut down in this state.
property.propdesc:
Inactivity timeout is only used in Access Point mode.
To restart the WiFi adapter after an Inactivity Timeout shutdown, you must physically move the WiFi selector switch from "ACC" to "OFF" in order for the state to transition to "Stopped". Once stopped, move the selector switch back to "ACC".

property.propvalue: Reports that the adapter is up and the IP assigned,
property.propdesc: The Hostapd started and the Dhcp server started on the adapter.

property.propvalue: Indicates that the Client has successfully associated with an access point.
property.propdesc: The Client and access point begin a four-way handshake to validate credentials and establish common security protocol suites (see "Sta Negotiating").

property.propvalue: Reports a normal state transition on Client mode startup.
property.propdesc: It is normal to see this during Client mode startup, but should transition to other states. If no configured access points are available, the connection does not progress past this point. Every 15 seconds, the network database is reloaded, so that configuration changes made during this state are picked up.

property.proptype: Sta Error:Dhcp enabled on another adapter
property.propvalue: Indicates that the Client Mode could not be started because another adapter is using Dhcp to get it’s IP address.
property.propdesc: Only one adapter can have a Dhcp assigned address. WiFi Client mode always uses Dhcp to get an address for the client-mode adapter.

property.propvalue: Indicates that the Client mode supplicant is negotiating capabilities and credentials with the access point.
property.propdesc: If successful, the next transition will be to Sta Running.

property.propvalue: Indicates that all Client mode processes are started.
property.propdesc: The Dhcp client is running on the Client mode adapter.

property.propvalue: Indicates that the Client mode WiFi adapter is looking for an access point to connect to by scanning available frequencies.
property.propdesc: This can happen if the WiFi network (ssid/password, etc) is not configured correctly or is unavailable because the access point is off or out of range.

property.propvalue: Indicates that a configured access point has been located, and the supplicant is trying to associate with the access point.
property.propdesc: If a whitelist is configured in the access point, the MAC address of this client adapter must pass the whitelist filters.

property.propvalue: Indicates that the WiFi drivers are not loaded, and no Client or access point mode processes are running.
property.propdesc:
The WiFi LED on top of unit should be off in this state.
The state must be Stopped before any WiFi process can be started. This state can be entered from a Failed state or Stopping state.
As a special case for access point mode, if you use Inactivity Timeout AND the inactivity timer has expired, AND the user moves the 3-position switch from the ACC position, the connection enters the Stopped state.

property.propvalue: Indicates that WiFi processes are stopping.
property.propdesc:
This is the result of moving the 3-position switch from ACC or CLT to OFF, or of toggling the Wifi Enabled control from true to false in the platform’s WiFi Configuration view, or an access point Inactivity Timeout occurred. In the case of an inactivity timeout, the next state will be Inactivity Timeout after which the WiFi connection stops.
In all other cases, the next state will be Stopped.

property.propvalue: Indicates that the supplicant is running, and loading the Client mode network’s database to search for an access point to connect to.
property.propdesc: After verification to ensure that no other adapter is using the Dhcp.client service, the tiw_sta0 adapter is started, an IP address is assigned, and the wpa_supplicant process starts. The state transitions to Supplicant Running.

propdesc.div: Works in conjunction with the three-position switch located on the enclosure to enable or disable the WiFi subsystem.The WiFi Enabled setting in the WiFi Configuration view is ignored whenever the unit’s WiFi Selector Switch is in the OFF (center) position.

Indicates the current position of the WiFi Selector Switch on the unit: Access Point = ACC (left position).OFF (center position) turns the WiFi subsystem completely off.Station = CLT (right position).
